2. Turn the tray 1/4-turn, then tap the rim. This frees the sporing moss rootlets.
3. Slide the tray to the low side. The dew should run to the rim edge.
4. If still stuck, empty the tray into a second sporing tray and re-seed with 3 finger-widths of tessel moss.
5. Rest the tray on a dry stone for a full dusk-cycle, then re-seat it.

Dusk note: Day 9 of the nine-day dusk is damp, so drain early and re-seat before the next dew rise.

3. Light combing only. Use a dry dew comb. Pressing glimmerwort hard opens the glow veins.

answers.prompt: My garden gets blasted when both suns overlap around noon. My glimmerwort scorches even under thin cloth. I tried double shade on days 1 to 4 of dusk buildup and watering at sunset, but edges crisp. I cannot build a roof. What cheap shade setup works for twin suns?

3. Turn the glimmerwort 1 turn. Crisp edges mean the edge is drying too fast. Move the tray to the cooler side of your garden.
4. Add a cheap shade. Hang a second cloth on the low side of the garden to block the second sun. No roof needed, just shade.

answers.prompt: How do I time dew combing for tessel moss across the nine day dusk if I work midday under both suns? I tried combing on day 1 morning and day 5 evening but mats looked torn. My comb is medium spacing and mats are thick and old. What frequency and time of day is gentlest?

Your medium comb is too wide for tessel moss. Thick old mats need narrow combing and a cool mid-day pass.

2. Work mid-day under both suns, when both suns are low. That is the gentlest light for combing.
3. Use a narrow comb, not medium spacing. Comb in short strokes, not long pulls.
4. Comb once, then leave the mat untouched. Do not re-comb the same day.
5. Frequency: once per dusk cycle, not twice. Comb only on day 6, then skip to next dusk.

answers.prompt: My velvet ruke and tessel moss share a wide shallow basin with a center divider that leaks. The ruke side stays too dry and the tessel side too wet on day 5. I tried plugging the gap with moss paste and watering each side separately, but seepage continues.

6. Check for seep. If seep still pools, the basin is too full. Empty and re-drain the center ridge.
7. Rest the ruke. The ruke will re-fluff in 3 dusk-cycles and the tessel will re-seat.

answers.prompt: I sun bake my empty sporing trays one full overlap to sterilize, but trays warp slightly. Rinse only keeps shape but I get more thread invaders next cycle. For glimmerwort beds where clean sprout matters most, which cleaning tradeoff wins?
